items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: And so my influences actually came out of King Oliver of Louis Armstrong, Paul Mares and Bix Beiderbecke.

ctx.x: Oh yes. And that was the influence. And then, at first. And we used to copy their numbers off the records. But we never would copy their solos. You had to play your own solo. We made that one of our rules that we all had, in other words we could play the ensemble the way Louis or King played them or Paul Mares. But then we had to play your own solos. You had to do your own individual solo the way you feel.

And we, that's the way we did until we heard the next record that came out a few months later, it was the Wolverines. And the cornet player was Bix Beiderbecke. Well he had such beautiful tone you know, that man I said that tone is lovely, that's the tone for me. And so my influences actually came out of King Oliver of Louis Armstrong, Paul Mares and Bix Beiderbecke.
